NGSS:MS-PS1-1.cc_advanced: I can build models of different molecules and extended structures and explain how the arrangement of atoms is linked to a property of the substance.
NGSS:MS-PS1-1.cc_at_target: I can develop models to show the atoms that make up simple molecules and extended structures.
NGSS:MS-PS1-1.cc_approaching: I can use a given model or kit to show how atoms join to make a simple molecule, with help.
NGSS:MS-PS1-1.cc_emerging: I can say that all matter is made of tiny particles called atoms, using a picture or model.

NGSS:MS-PS1-2.cc_advanced: I can design a test to collect property data before and after substances mix and use the data to justify whether a chemical reaction happened.
NGSS:MS-PS1-2.cc_at_target: I can analyze data on properties of substances before and after they interact to decide if a chemical reaction has occurred.
NGSS:MS-PS1-2.cc_approaching: I can compare one or two properties, like color or smell, before and after mixing, using a data table and sentence frames.
NGSS:MS-PS1-2.cc_emerging: I can name some signs of a chemical change, such as bubbles, color change, or heat, with picture support.

NGSS:MS-PS1-3.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how a synthetic material made from a natural resource benefits and harms society and suggest a way to reduce the harm.
NGSS:MS-PS1-3.cc_at_target: I can gather information to describe how synthetic materials come from natural resources and how they impact society.
NGSS:MS-PS1-3.cc_approaching: I can match a synthetic material, like plastic, to the natural resource it comes from, using a text with support.
NGSS:MS-PS1-3.cc_emerging: I can sort materials into natural and human-made, using pictures and a word bank.

NGSS:MS-PS1-4.cc_advanced: I can use a particle model to predict and explain changes in temperature and state for a new substance, such as wax or chocolate, when heat is added or removed.
NGSS:MS-PS1-4.cc_at_target: I can develop a model that predicts and describes how particle motion, temperature, and state change when thermal energy is added or removed.
NGSS:MS-PS1-4.cc_approaching: I can draw particles in a solid, liquid, and gas and say how they move faster when heated, with a model to guide me.
NGSS:MS-PS1-4.cc_emerging: I can name solids, liquids, and gases and say that heating can melt or boil a substance, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-PS1-5.cc_advanced: I can use a model and real mass data to explain why mass seems to change in an open container but stays the same in a closed one.
NGSS:MS-PS1-5.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to show that atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed, in a chemical reaction, so mass is conserved.
NGSS:MS-PS1-5.cc_approaching: I can count atoms on each side of a simple reaction model and say if they match, with step-by-step support.
NGSS:MS-PS1-5.cc_emerging: I can say that matter is made of atoms and that atoms can join in new ways, using models or drawings.

NGSS:MS-PS1-6.cc_advanced: I can test and improve my device several times, using data to explain how changing the amount or type of chemical changes the energy released or absorbed.
NGSS:MS-PS1-6.cc_at_target: I can design, build, test, and modify a device that releases or absorbs thermal energy through a chemical process.
NGSS:MS-PS1-6.cc_approaching: I can follow a plan to build a hot or cold pack and record its temperature change, with help to improve it.
NGSS:MS-PS1-6.cc_emerging: I can notice that some mixtures get hot or cold when they react, using a thermometer with support.

NGSS:MS-PS2-1.cc_advanced: I can design and test a solution for a collision problem and use Newton's Third Law to explain why my design protects the objects better than others.
NGSS:MS-PS2-1.cc_at_target: I can apply Newton's Third Law to design a solution to a problem involving two colliding objects.
NGSS:MS-PS2-1.cc_approaching: I can describe that when two objects collide they push on each other with equal and opposite forces, using a diagram and frames.
NGSS:MS-PS2-1.cc_emerging: I can show with my hands or objects that a push in one direction causes a push back, with teacher support.

NGSS:MS-PS2-2.cc_advanced: I can plan a fair test that changes force or mass, collect data, and use it to predict the motion of a new object.
NGSS:MS-PS2-2.cc_at_target: I can plan an investigation to show that an object's change in motion depends on the total forces on it and its mass.
NGSS:MS-PS2-2.cc_approaching: I can follow an investigation plan and describe how a bigger push or a heavier object changes motion, with support.
NGSS:MS-PS2-2.cc_emerging: I can say that a push or pull can start, stop, or change the direction of an object, using real objects.

NGSS:MS-PS2-3.cc_advanced: I can ask testable questions about electric and magnetic forces, analyze data, and design a device, such as a stronger electromagnet, based on my findings.
NGSS:MS-PS2-3.cc_at_target: I can ask questions about data to find the factors that affect the strength of electric and magnetic forces.
NGSS:MS-PS2-3.cc_approaching: I can ask a simple question about magnets or static electricity and read a data table to answer it, with help.
NGSS:MS-PS2-3.cc_emerging: I can observe that magnets attract some objects and that charged objects can attract paper, with support.

NGSS:MS-PS2-4.cc_advanced: I can use data from simulations to argue how both mass and distance affect gravitational force and apply this to orbits in the solar system.
NGSS:MS-PS2-4.cc_at_target: I can construct and present an argument with evidence that gravitational forces are attractive and depend on the masses of the objects.
NGSS:MS-PS2-4.cc_approaching: I can explain that gravity pulls objects toward each other and that bigger masses pull more, using a chart and sentence frames.
NGSS:MS-PS2-4.cc_emerging: I can say that gravity pulls things down toward Earth, using a demonstration or picture.

NGSS:MS-PS2-5.cc_advanced: I can design and critique an investigation that maps a field and explain how the evidence shows forces act without contact.
NGSS:MS-PS2-5.cc_at_target: I can conduct an investigation and evaluate its design to show that fields exist between objects that exert forces without touching.
NGSS:MS-PS2-5.cc_approaching: I can carry out a guided investigation with magnets and describe that they push or pull without touching, with support.
NGSS:MS-PS2-5.cc_emerging: I can observe that a magnet can move a paperclip without touching it, with teacher guidance.

NGSS:MS-PS3-1.cc_advanced: I can use graphs to compare how doubling mass and doubling speed affect kinetic energy and explain which change has the bigger effect.
NGSS:MS-PS3-1.cc_at_target: I can construct and interpret graphs of data to describe how kinetic energy relates to an object's mass and to its speed.
NGSS:MS-PS3-1.cc_approaching: I can read a simple graph and say that faster or heavier objects have more motion energy, with sentence frames.
NGSS:MS-PS3-1.cc_emerging: I can say that moving objects have energy and that faster objects have more, using real examples.

NGSS:MS-PS3-2.cc_advanced: I can use a model to compare potential energy stored in gravitational, magnetic, and electric systems and predict what happens when distances change.
NGSS:MS-PS3-2.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to describe that changing the distance between interacting objects changes the potential energy stored in the system.
NGSS:MS-PS3-2.cc_approaching: I can use a diagram to show that lifting an object higher stores more energy, with guided support.
NGSS:MS-PS3-2.cc_emerging: I can say that a raised object or stretched spring has stored energy, using a demonstration.

NGSS:MS-PS3-3.cc_advanced: I can test and redesign my device using temperature data and explain how each material choice reduces or increases heat transfer.
NGSS:MS-PS3-3.cc_at_target: I can apply science ideas to design, build, and test a device that minimizes or maximizes thermal energy transfer.
NGSS:MS-PS3-3.cc_approaching: I can choose materials to keep something hot or cold and test my device with a thermometer, with help.
NGSS:MS-PS3-3.cc_emerging: I can sort materials that keep things warm or cool, such as foam and metal, with picture support.

NGSS:MS-PS3-4.cc_advanced: I can plan and carry out an investigation, control variables, and use my results to predict temperature changes for different materials and masses.
NGSS:MS-PS3-4.cc_at_target: I can plan an investigation to find how energy transferred, type of matter, mass, and temperature change are related.
NGSS:MS-PS3-4.cc_approaching: I can follow a plan to heat or cool water samples and record temperature changes in a table, with support.
NGSS:MS-PS3-4.cc_emerging: I can use a thermometer to read the temperature of hot and cold water, with help.

NGSS:MS-PS3-5.cc_advanced: I can use an energy diagram and data to argue where energy goes in a real event, such as a car braking, and account for all of it.
NGSS:MS-PS3-5.cc_at_target: I can construct and present an argument that when an object's kinetic energy changes, energy is transferred to or from the object.
NGSS:MS-PS3-5.cc_approaching: I can describe how energy moves when a ball speeds up or slows down, using a diagram and sentence frames.
NGSS:MS-PS3-5.cc_emerging: I can say that energy can move from one object to another, like when a ball hits another ball.

NGSS:MS-PS4-1.cc_advanced: I can use math to compare two waves and explain how changing amplitude changes the energy, using an example such as sound volume.
NGSS:MS-PS4-1.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical representations to describe a wave model and show how amplitude is related to the energy in a wave.
NGSS:MS-PS4-1.cc_approaching: I can label amplitude and wavelength on a wave diagram and say that bigger waves carry more energy, with support.
NGSS:MS-PS4-1.cc_emerging: I can draw a wave and point to its top and bottom, using a model.

NGSS:MS-PS4-2.cc_advanced: I can use a model to predict and explain how light or sound will behave when it meets a new material, such as glass, water, or foam.
NGSS:MS-PS4-2.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to describe how waves are reflected, absorbed, or transmitted through different materials.
NGSS:MS-PS4-2.cc_approaching: I can sort materials by whether light passes through, bounces off, or is absorbed, using a diagram with help.
NGSS:MS-PS4-2.cc_emerging: I can observe that light bounces off a mirror and passes through clear materials, with teacher support.

NGSS:MS-PS4-3.cc_advanced: I can evaluate sources and explain, with examples from phones or the internet, why digital signals are more reliable than analog signals.
NGSS:MS-PS4-3.cc_at_target: I can combine scientific and technical information to support the claim that digital signals encode and send information more reliably than analog signals.
NGSS:MS-PS4-3.cc_approaching: I can compare a digital and an analog signal using pictures and say which is clearer, with sentence frames.
NGSS:MS-PS4-3.cc_emerging: I can name devices that send information, such as phones and radios, with picture support.

NGSS:MS-LS1-1.cc_advanced: I can use a microscope investigation to compare different cell types and explain how the evidence shows all living things are made of cells.
NGSS:MS-LS1-1.cc_at_target: I can conduct an investigation to provide evidence that living things are made of one cell or many different cells.
NGSS:MS-LS1-1.cc_approaching: I can observe cells under a microscope and label them as one cell or many cells, with guidance.
NGSS:MS-LS1-1.cc_emerging: I can sort living and non-living things and say that living things are made of cells, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-LS1-2.cc_advanced: I can use a model to predict what would happen to a cell if one part, such as the mitochondria or membrane, stopped working.
NGSS:MS-LS1-2.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to describe how a cell works as a whole and how its parts help it function.
NGSS:MS-LS1-2.cc_approaching: I can label the main parts of a cell and match each part to its job, using a word bank.
NGSS:MS-LS1-2.cc_emerging: I can point to the nucleus and cell membrane on a cell picture, with support.

NGSS:MS-LS1-3.cc_advanced: I can argue with evidence how two body systems work together, such as the circulatory and respiratory systems during exercise.
NGSS:MS-LS1-3.cc_at_target: I can use evidence to argue that the body is a system of interacting subsystems made of groups of cells.
NGSS:MS-LS1-3.cc_approaching: I can put cells, tissues, organs, and systems in order and give one example of each, with a graphic organizer.
NGSS:MS-LS1-3.cc_emerging: I can name some body organs, like the heart and lungs, and say what they do, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-LS1-4.cc_advanced: I can evaluate evidence for several animal behaviors and plant structures and explain which most increases the chance of successful reproduction.
NGSS:MS-LS1-4.cc_at_target: I can use evidence and reasoning to explain how animal behaviors and plant structures affect the chance of successful reproduction.
NGSS:MS-LS1-4.cc_approaching: I can give an example of an animal behavior or flower part that helps reproduction and explain it with sentence frames.
NGSS:MS-LS1-4.cc_emerging: I can name ways animals care for young or how flowers attract bees, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-LS1-5.cc_advanced: I can analyze data to separate genetic and environmental effects on growth and explain a real example, such as plant growth in drought.
NGSS:MS-LS1-5.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence for how environmental and genetic factors affect the growth of organisms.
NGSS:MS-LS1-5.cc_approaching: I can use a data table to describe how water, light, or food changed how a plant or animal grew, with support.
NGSS:MS-LS1-5.cc_emerging: I can say that living things need food, water, and light to grow, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-LS1-6.cc_advanced: I can use evidence to explain how photosynthesis links matter and energy between plants, animals, and the air in an ecosystem.
NGSS:MS-LS1-6.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence for the role of photosynthesis in cycling matter and energy into and out of organisms.
NGSS:MS-LS1-6.cc_approaching: I can complete a diagram showing that plants use light, water, and carbon dioxide to make sugar and oxygen, with a word bank.
NGSS:MS-LS1-6.cc_emerging: I can say that plants need sunlight, water, and air to make their own food, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-LS1-7.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how the same atoms from food are used both to build body parts and to release energy.
NGSS:MS-LS1-7.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to describe how food is rearranged through chemical reactions to make new molecules for growth or to release energy.
NGSS:MS-LS1-7.cc_approaching: I can use a diagram to show that food is broken down in the body to give energy and help growth, with support.
NGSS:MS-LS1-7.cc_emerging: I can say that food gives our bodies energy and helps us grow, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-LS1-8.cc_advanced: I can combine information from several sources to explain how a sense receptor, nerves, and the brain work together in a fast reaction and in memory.
NGSS:MS-LS1-8.cc_at_target: I can gather and combine information that sensory receptors respond to stimuli and send messages to the brain for actions or memories.
NGSS:MS-LS1-8.cc_approaching: I can describe how a sense organ, like the eye, sends a message to the brain, using a flow chart with help.
NGSS:MS-LS1-8.cc_emerging: I can name the five senses and the body part for each, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-LS2-1.cc_advanced: I can analyze population graphs to predict what will happen to organisms when a resource changes and explain my reasoning with data.
NGSS:MS-LS2-1.cc_at_target: I can analyze and interpret data to show how resource availability affects organisms and populations in an ecosystem.
NGSS:MS-LS2-1.cc_approaching: I can read a simple graph and say how a population changed when food or water changed, with sentence frames.
NGSS:MS-LS2-1.cc_emerging: I can name resources that living things need, such as food, water, and space, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-LS2-2.cc_advanced: I can predict interactions in an unfamiliar ecosystem and justify my prediction using patterns of competition, predation, and mutualism.
NGSS:MS-LS2-2.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation that predicts patterns of interactions among organisms in different ecosystems.
NGSS:MS-LS2-2.cc_approaching: I can identify predator and prey, competition, or helping relationships in an ecosystem picture, with a word bank.
NGSS:MS-LS2-2.cc_emerging: I can say which animal eats which in a simple food chain, with picture support.

NGSS:MS-LS2-3.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain what happens to matter and energy if decomposers or producers are removed from an ecosystem.
NGSS:MS-LS2-3.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to describe how matter cycles and energy flows among living and nonliving parts of an ecosystem.
NGSS:MS-LS2-3.cc_approaching: I can draw a food web with producers, consumers, and decomposers and show the direction of energy, with support.
NGSS:MS-LS2-3.cc_emerging: I can make a simple food chain starting with the sun and a plant, using picture cards.

NGSS:MS-LS2-4.cc_advanced: I can evaluate data from a real ecosystem change, such as coral bleaching in the Gulf, and argue how it affects several populations.
NGSS:MS-LS2-4.cc_at_target: I can construct an argument supported by evidence that changes to physical or biological parts of an ecosystem affect populations.
NGSS:MS-LS2-4.cc_approaching: I can use data to describe how one change, like less rain, affected a population, with sentence frames.
NGSS:MS-LS2-4.cc_emerging: I can say that living things can be harmed when their habitat changes, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-LS2-5.cc_advanced: I can compare design solutions for protecting an ecosystem, using criteria, constraints, and data, and recommend the best one with reasons.
NGSS:MS-LS2-5.cc_at_target: I can evaluate competing design solutions for maintaining biodiversity and ecosystem services.
NGSS:MS-LS2-5.cc_approaching: I can compare two ways to protect a habitat and say which is better using a simple checklist, with support.
NGSS:MS-LS2-5.cc_emerging: I can name ways people help protect plants and animals, such as planting trees, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-LS3-1.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how one specific mutation changes a protein and predict whether its effect is harmful, helpful, or neutral.
NGSS:MS-LS3-1.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to describe why changes to genes (mutations) may change proteins and cause harmful, helpful, or neutral effects.
NGSS:MS-LS3-1.cc_approaching: I can explain with a diagram that genes are instructions and a change in a gene can change a trait, with support.
NGSS:MS-LS3-1.cc_emerging: I can say that living things get traits from their parents, using pictures of families of animals.

NGSS:MS-LS3-2.cc_advanced: I can use Punnett squares to predict offspring traits and explain why sexual reproduction gives a population more variation.
NGSS:MS-LS3-2.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to explain why asexual reproduction gives identical offspring and sexual reproduction gives offspring with variation.
NGSS:MS-LS3-2.cc_approaching: I can compare pictures of asexual and sexual reproduction and say which offspring look the same as the parent, with help.
NGSS:MS-LS3-2.cc_emerging: I can say that babies look like their parents but not exactly the same, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-LS4-1.cc_advanced: I can analyze fossil data from rock layers to describe patterns of change and extinction and explain how scientists date them.
NGSS:MS-LS4-1.cc_at_target: I can analyze and interpret fossil record data for patterns of existence, diversity, extinction, and change of life on Earth.
NGSS:MS-LS4-1.cc_approaching: I can use a rock layer diagram to say which fossils are older or younger, with support.
NGSS:MS-LS4-1.cc_emerging: I can say that fossils are remains of living things from long ago, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-LS4-2.cc_advanced: I can compare anatomical structures across several modern and fossil organisms and justify which are most closely related.
NGSS:MS-LS4-2.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation for anatomical similarities and differences among modern and fossil organisms to infer evolutionary relationships.
NGSS:MS-LS4-2.cc_approaching: I can compare bones of two animals and describe one way they are alike and one way they differ, with a diagram.
NGSS:MS-LS4-2.cc_emerging: I can point out body parts that look alike in two animals, such as a human arm and a bat wing.

NGSS:MS-LS4-3.cc_advanced: I can analyze embryo pictures from several species and explain how the patterns show relationships that adult forms hide.
NGSS:MS-LS4-3.cc_at_target: I can analyze pictures of embryos from different species to compare patterns and identify relationships not seen in adult anatomy.
NGSS:MS-LS4-3.cc_approaching: I can compare two embryo pictures and describe features that are the same, with a word bank.
NGSS:MS-LS4-3.cc_emerging: I can notice that young animals at an early stage can look alike, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-LS4-4.cc_advanced: I can use data and probability to explain how a trait spreads in a population over generations in a changing environment.
NGSS:MS-LS4-4.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation with evidence of how genetic variations in traits help some individuals survive and reproduce in a specific environment.
NGSS:MS-LS4-4.cc_approaching: I can explain why an animal with a helpful trait, like camouflage, is more likely to survive, using sentence frames.
NGSS:MS-LS4-4.cc_emerging: I can notice that animals of the same kind can look different, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-LS4-5.cc_advanced: I can evaluate sources about a technology such as selective breeding or genetic modification and discuss its benefits and risks.
NGSS:MS-LS4-5.cc_at_target: I can gather and combine information about technologies that have changed how humans influence the inheritance of desired traits.
NGSS:MS-LS4-5.cc_approaching: I can describe one example of selective breeding, such as date palms or camels, using a short text with support.
NGSS:MS-LS4-5.cc_emerging: I can say that farmers choose the best plants and animals to grow, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-LS4-6.cc_advanced: I can use a simulation and graphs to model how natural selection changes trait percentages and predict future changes.
NGSS:MS-LS4-6.cc_at_target: I can use mathematical representations to support explanations of how natural selection increases or decreases traits in populations over time.
NGSS:MS-LS4-6.cc_approaching: I can read a bar graph to describe how the number of animals with a trait changed over time, with support.
NGSS:MS-LS4-6.cc_emerging: I can count animals with and without a trait in a picture and record it in a table, with help.

NGSS:MS-ESS1-1.cc_advanced: I can use a model to predict moon phases and eclipses and explain why seasons in Qatar differ from seasons in the southern hemisphere.
NGSS:MS-ESS1-1.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model of the Earth-sun-moon system to describe patterns of lunar phases, eclipses, and seasons.
NGSS:MS-ESS1-1.cc_approaching: I can use a physical model to show how the moon orbits Earth and name the main moon phases, with support.
NGSS:MS-ESS1-1.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth spins and moves around the sun and the moon moves around Earth, using a model.

NGSS:MS-ESS1-2.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how gravity keeps planets in orbit and predict what would happen if the sun's gravity were weaker.
NGSS:MS-ESS1-2.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to describe the role of gravity in the motions within galaxies and the solar system.
NGSS:MS-ESS1-2.cc_approaching: I can use a diagram to explain that gravity keeps planets moving around the sun, with sentence frames.
NGSS:MS-ESS1-2.cc_emerging: I can name the sun and planets and say that planets move around the sun, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-ESS1-3.cc_advanced: I can analyze data to compare planets and moons and build a scale model that shows sizes and distances.
NGSS:MS-ESS1-3.cc_at_target: I can analyze and interpret data to determine scale properties of objects in the solar system.
NGSS:MS-ESS1-3.cc_approaching: I can read a data table to compare the size or distance of two planets, with support.
NGSS:MS-ESS1-3.cc_emerging: I can sort solar system objects from smallest to largest using pictures, with help.

NGSS:MS-ESS1-4.cc_advanced: I can use rock layer and fossil evidence to place major events on the geologic time scale and explain how scientists know their order.
NGSS:MS-ESS1-4.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence from rock layers for how the geologic time scale organizes Earth's 4.6-billion-year history.
NGSS:MS-ESS1-4.cc_approaching: I can put events from Earth's history in order on a timeline using rock layer clues, with support.
NGSS:MS-ESS1-4.cc_emerging: I can say that lower rock layers are usually older than upper layers, using a diagram.

NGSS:MS-ESS2-1.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how energy from the sun and Earth's interior drives the rock cycle and predict how a rock will change.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-1.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to describe how Earth's materials cycle and the energy flow that drives this process.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-1.cc_approaching: I can complete a rock cycle diagram and name the processes, such as melting and weathering, with a word bank.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-1.cc_emerging: I can name the three types of rock, using pictures and samples.

NGSS:MS-ESS2-2.cc_advanced: I can compare fast and slow geoscience processes with evidence and explain how both shaped a real landform, such as wadis or sand dunes.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-2.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence for how geoscience processes have changed Earth's surface at different time and space scales.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-2.cc_approaching: I can describe how wind, water, or earthquakes change land, using pictures and sentence frames.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-2.cc_emerging: I can say that wind and water can move sand and rock, using a demonstration.

NGSS:MS-ESS2-3.cc_advanced: I can combine fossil, rock, and seafloor data to argue how continents moved and predict future plate motions.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-3.cc_at_target: I can analyze and interpret data on fossils, rocks, continent shapes, and seafloor structures to show evidence of past plate motions.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-3.cc_approaching: I can fit continent shapes together like a puzzle and describe matching fossils, with support.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-3.cc_emerging: I can say that Earth's continents are on large moving pieces, using a map.

NGSS:MS-ESS2-4.cc_advanced: I can use a model of the water cycle to explain how the sun and gravity drive each step and apply it to water in Qatar.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-4.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to describe how water cycles through Earth's systems, driven by energy from the sun and the force of gravity.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-4.cc_approaching: I can label evaporation, condensation, and precipitation on a water cycle diagram, with a word bank.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-4.cc_emerging: I can say that water can be liquid, solid, or gas and that rain comes from clouds, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-ESS2-5.cc_advanced: I can collect and analyze weather data to explain how moving air masses caused a weather change and predict the next day's weather.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-5.cc_at_target: I can collect data to provide evidence for how motions and interactions of air masses cause changes in weather.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-5.cc_approaching: I can record temperature and wind data for several days and describe a change, with a data table.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-5.cc_emerging: I can describe today's weather using words like hot, windy, or humid, with picture support.

NGSS:MS-ESS2-6.cc_advanced: I can use a model to explain how unequal heating, Earth's rotation, and ocean currents together create the climate of a region such as the Gulf.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-6.cc_at_target: I can develop and use a model to describe how unequal heating and Earth's rotation cause atmospheric and ocean circulation that shapes regional climates.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-6.cc_approaching: I can use a diagram to show that the equator gets more heat than the poles and that this moves air, with support.
NGSS:MS-ESS2-6.cc_emerging: I can say that some places on Earth are hot and some are cold, using a globe or map.

NGSS:MS-ESS3-1.cc_advanced: I can explain with evidence why oil, gas, and groundwater are found in some places, such as Qatar, and not others, and how use changes their supply.
NGSS:MS-ESS3-1.cc_at_target: I can construct an explanation based on evidence for how uneven distributions of minerals, energy, and groundwater result from past and current geoscience processes.
NGSS:MS-ESS3-1.cc_approaching: I can use a map to show where a resource like oil or water is found and say one reason why, with support.
NGSS:MS-ESS3-1.cc_emerging: I can name natural resources, such as water, oil, and gas, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-ESS3-2.cc_advanced: I can analyze hazard data to forecast a future event and evaluate which technology would best reduce its effects.
NGSS:MS-ESS3-2.cc_at_target: I can analyze and interpret data on natural hazards to forecast future events and inform technologies that reduce their effects.
NGSS:MS-ESS3-2.cc_approaching: I can read a hazard map or graph and describe where or when a hazard is likely, with sentence frames.
NGSS:MS-ESS3-2.cc_emerging: I can name natural hazards, such as sandstorms, floods, and earthquakes, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-ESS3-3.cc_advanced: I can design, test, and improve a method to monitor and reduce a local human impact, such as plastic waste on beaches, using data.
NGSS:MS-ESS3-3.cc_at_target: I can apply scientific principles to design a method for monitoring and minimizing a human impact on the environment.
NGSS:MS-ESS3-3.cc_approaching: I can choose a human impact and suggest one way to measure it and one way to reduce it, with a planning template.
NGSS:MS-ESS3-3.cc_emerging: I can name ways people harm the environment, such as littering, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-ESS3-4.cc_advanced: I can use data to argue how population growth and resource use affect several Earth systems and propose ways to reduce the impact.
NGSS:MS-ESS3-4.cc_at_target: I can construct an argument supported by evidence for how growing human population and resource use per person impact Earth's systems.
NGSS:MS-ESS3-4.cc_approaching: I can use a graph to describe how more people use more water or energy, with sentence frames.
NGSS:MS-ESS3-4.cc_emerging: I can say that people use water, food, and energy every day, using pictures.

NGSS:MS-ESS3-5.cc_advanced: I can ask and refine questions to evaluate evidence for human and natural causes of rising temperatures and identify which evidence is strongest.
NGSS:MS-ESS3-5.cc_at_target: I can ask questions to clarify evidence of the factors that have caused the rise in global temperatures over the past century.
NGSS:MS-ESS3-5.cc_approaching: I can ask a question about a temperature graph and name one cause of warming, with question stems.
NGSS:MS-ESS3-5.cc_emerging: I can read a thermometer and say whether it is getting hotter, using a simple graph with help.

NGSS:MS-ETS1-1.cc_advanced: I can define a design problem with precise, measurable criteria and constraints and explain how science ideas and impacts on people and nature shape them.
NGSS:MS-ETS1-1.cc_at_target: I can define the criteria and constraints of a design problem precisely, considering science principles and impacts on people and the environment.
NGSS:MS-ETS1-1.cc_approaching: I can list what a design must do (criteria) and its limits (constraints), using a template.
NGSS:MS-ETS1-1.cc_emerging: I can describe a problem that a new tool or object could solve, with teacher support.

NGSS:MS-ETS1-2.cc_advanced: I can build a weighted decision matrix to compare designs and justify which best meets the criteria and constraints.
NGSS:MS-ETS1-2.cc_at_target: I can evaluate competing design solutions using a systematic process to see how well they meet the criteria and constraints.
NGSS:MS-ETS1-2.cc_approaching: I can use a checklist to compare two designs against the criteria, with support.
NGSS:MS-ETS1-2.cc_emerging: I can say which of two designs I like better and give one reason, using sentence frames.

NGSS:MS-ETS1-3.cc_advanced: I can analyze test data from several designs and combine their best features into a new design that performs better.
NGSS:MS-ETS1-3.cc_at_target: I can analyze test data to find similarities and differences among designs and combine the best features into a new solution.
NGSS:MS-ETS1-3.cc_approaching: I can read test results for two designs and say which part of each worked best, with a data table.
NGSS:MS-ETS1-3.cc_emerging: I can test a design and say whether it worked, with teacher guidance.

NGSS:MS-ETS1-4.cc_advanced: I can use a model to generate data, run several rounds of testing, and justify how each change moved my design closer to optimal.
NGSS:MS-ETS1-4.cc_at_target: I can develop a model to generate data for testing and improving a proposed object, tool, or process until an optimal design is reached.
NGSS:MS-ETS1-4.cc_approaching: I can build and test a model, record results, and make one improvement, with step-by-step support.
NGSS:MS-ETS1-4.cc_emerging: I can build a simple model of my idea using provided materials, with help.
